application.name: ofetch
application.summary: Typed HTTP client for JavaScript/TypeScript that wraps fetch with automatic JSON serialization, typed responses, retries, timeouts, hooks, and normalized errors.
application.purpose: Provide a small, strongly typed fetch-style API for making HTTP requests across browser and Node.js runtimes, with developer-friendly ergonomics such as baseURL/params/query support, automatic body/header handling, retry/timeout controls, and structured response parsing.

domains.description: Normalized FetchError creation and lifecycle decisions around aborts, retries, and HTTP error responses.

domains.name: Node.js runtime support
domains.description: Node-specific fetch injection, optional keep-alive agents, and node-fetch-native fallback.

domains.name: Examples, playground and tests

terminology.meaning: The main typed HTTP client instance, callable like fetch but returning parsed data with TypeScript typing; has .raw, .native and .create variants.
Per-request context object carrying request, options, response, and error.
Per-request options: baseURL, params, query, headers, body, timeout, retry, retryDelay, retryStatusCodes, responseType, parseResponse, ignoreResponseError, duplex, and lifecycle hooks.
PATCH, POST, PUT and DELETE; used to decide default retry counts and body serialization.
Heuristic for detecting values that can be safely JSON-stringified as request bodies.
Content-Type based selection of the parser: json, text or blob.
Deep merge of default options and per-call options, including params, query and headers.
Invokes a single hook or an array of hooks against the fetch context.
Normalized error exposing method/url request, status/statusText/data from response, and original error cause.
Automatic re-request policy; defaults to retryable statuses such as 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, with default retry count of 0 for payload methods and 1 otherwise.
Abort signals a fetch after a timeout is exceeded, producing a TimeoutError with code 23.
Option that prevents 4xx/5xx responses from throwing, allowing callers to handle them manually.
URL composition inputs for request construction and merging.
HTTP statuses 101, 204, 205 and 304 that are treated as having no body to parse.

applicationFacts: The package is a typed fetch wrapper, exposing both ofetch and $fetch aliases plus .raw, .native and .create variants.
There are two entry points: src/index.ts for browser/global fetch and src/node.ts for Node.js.
src/node.ts can enable keep-alive agents via the FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable; otherwise it uses node-fetch-native as the base fetch.
createFetch accepts globalOptions (fetch, Headers, AbortController, defaults) and exposes $fetch.create for scoped instances that merge defaults.
Request bodies are JSON-stringified automatically when the method is a payload method and the body is JSON-serializable, with application/json content-type and accept defaults.
ReadableStream and Node.js Readable request bodies are passed through and set duplex=half automatically when needed.
Response parsing skips null-body statuses (101, 204, 205, 304) and HEAD requests.
Response type is chosen from Content-Type, can be forced via responseType, and parseResponse overrides JSON parsing to use a custom parser.
Retry is disabled for active aborts; otherwise retried when response status matches retryStatusCodes (default 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504).
Retry policy: number of retries uses the configured number, otherwise payload methods default to 0 and non-payload methods default to 1.
Retry delay can be a fixed number or a callback receiving the FetchContext.
Timeout is enforced by aborting the request after the configured timeout; the cause becomes a TimeoutError with code 23 (DOMException.TIMEOUT_ERR).
HTTP 4xx/5xx responses throw by default unless ignoreResponseError is set; onResponse and onResponseError hooks run around response handling.
Lifecycle hooks (onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError) accept a single hook or an array of hooks and run sequentially.
Options are merged across defaults and per-call options, with deep-merging for params, query and Headers.
Errors are normalized into FetchError via createFetchError, exposing request, options, response, data, status, statusText/statusMessage via getters.
Tests use a local h3/listhen server and vitest, covering parsing, retries, aborts, hooks, custom parseResponse, and deep option merging.
